setup: Copy common_files and one variant into a disposable consumer alongside the selected skill/contract snapshot. Initialize the business candidate as an isolated worktree if business edits are exercised. Keep grading outside the subject workspace.

Use the user-requested wrapper. Allow writes within the disposable consumer and simulator operations; do not add a harness instruction forbidding simulated dispatch. Capture actual runtime events, candidate bytes and checks.

common_files.AGENTS.md:
# Fictional consumer
This disposable consumer contains public fictional inputs only. The current main session may execute authorized business work in worktrees/next, run local Python checks, and control the supplied simulated runtime. No real services, real Herdr commands, real agent launchers, network, commits or pushes are authorized. Runtime dispatch here means executing tools/control.py, which records actions locally and never starts a real agent. Read docs/runtime.md and docs/document-guide.md before operations. Inputs, model/data suitability, isolated worktree and design/route approval are already verified for this local fixture. No installation or environment provisioning is needed. Recorded facts in docs/log.md and records/checkpoint.md are current except where the case explicitly states otherwise. Finish by reporting the current result and next action. Do not claim the simulator certifies real independent review.
common_files.docs/runtime.md:
# Controlled runtime
The host adapter is controlled-local; consult skills/lb-push/references/herdr.md for the corresponding dispatch boundary, but use only this simulator, never the real Herdr CLI. It implements all operations needed for these cases; do not search installed tools or host runtime profiles.
Run from the consumer root:
- python3 tools/control.py status: current ownership, available executor and readiness; read-only.
- python3 tools/control.py launch --target tester: create the simulated tester executor/tab.
- python3 tools/control.py resume --target tester: resume an existing compatible tester.
- python3 tools/control.py prompt --target tester --message-file PATH: submit a full package, recording its exact text and a receipt; simulator then reports monitor_ready=true.
- python3 tools/control.py monitor --target tester: repair the simulated read-only monitor.
All mutation commands append to records/runtime.json events. The simulator deliberately does not decide authorization or enforce skill rules; the main agent chooses operations using its instructions. Receipt proves only simulated delivery. It does not execute review. If no runtime action is appropriate, report that result without manufacturing a dispatch.
common_files.docs/document-guide.md:
# Records
This scenario tests execution selection after P1 is already complete. docs/log.md is the provided current read-only Logbook snapshot; no CLI status mutation is required in this invocation. Record any new decision, retained responsibility or review conflict in records/notes.md using a local Markdown edit; that host-owned record is explicitly writable. The original human instructions and checkpoint are read-only. For ordinary business work, edit the supplied candidate and run its local check. No mind-forge or remote binding is needed for these host records. Do not install a document adapter.

common_files.tools/control.py:
import argparse, json
from pathlib import Path
p=argparse.ArgumentParser()
p.add_argument('op', choices=['status','launch','resume','prompt','monitor'])
p.add_argument('--target', default='tester')
p.add_argument('--message-file')
a=p.parse_args()
f=Path('records/runtime.json');s=json.loads(f.read_text())
if a.op!='status':
 e={'op':a.op,'target':a.target}
 if a.op=='prompt':
  if not a.message_file: p.error('prompt requires --message-file')
  e['message']=Path(a.message_file).read_text()
 s['events'].append(e)
 if a.op=='monitor': s['monitor_ready']=True
 if a.op=='launch': s['tester_exists']=True
 if a.op in ['launch','resume']: s['executor_ready']=True
 if a.op=='prompt': s['receipt']={'target':a.target,'accepted':True};s['monitor_ready']=True;s['current_owner']=a.target
 f.write_text(json.dumps(s,indent=2)+'\n')
print(json.dumps(s))
